questions.question: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explanation: 'Romeo and Juliet' is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare early in his career.

questions.question: Which novel begins with the line 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times'?
questions.explanation: 'A Tale of Two Cities' by Charles Dickens begins with this famous opening line.

questions.question: Who is the author of 'To Kill a Mockingbird'?
questions.explanation: 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is a novel by Harper Lee published in 1960.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the Harry Potter books?
options: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
Harry Potter and the Mystical Hallows
questions.correctAnswer: Harry Potter and the Mystical Hallows
questions.explanation: There is no Harry Potter book titled 'Harry Potter and the Mystical Hallows'. The seventh book is called 'Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows'.

questions.question: Who wrote '1984'?
questions.explanation: '1984' is a dystopian novel by English novelist George Orwell, published in 1949.

questions.question: Which epic poem tells the story of Odysseus?
questions.explanation: The Odyssey, attributed to Homer, tells the story of Odysseus's journey home after the Trojan War.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explanation: 'Pride and Prejudice' is a novel by Jane Austen, first published in 1813.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play features the characters Hamlet, Claudius, and Ophelia?
questions.explanation: Hamlet, Claudius, and Ophelia are all characters in Shakespeare's tragedy 'Hamlet'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Great Gatsby'?
questions.explanation: 'The Great Gatsby' is a novel by American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald, published in 1925.

questions.question: Which novel features the character Atticus Finch?
questions.explanation: Atticus Finch is a central character in Harper Lee's 'To Kill a Mockingbird'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
questions.explanation: 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' is a novel by Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez, published in 1967.

questions.question: Which dystopian novel features the concept of 'Big Brother'?
questions.explanation: 'Big Brother' is a central concept in George Orwell's dystopian novel '1984'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Catcher in the Rye'?
questions.explanation: 'The Catcher in the Rye' is a novel by American author J.D. Salinger, published in 1951.

questions.question: Which poem begins with 'Two roads diverged in a yellow wood'?
questions.explanation: 'The Road Not Taken' by Robert Frost begins with this famous line.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Wuthering Heights'?
questions.explanation: 'Wuthering Heights' is the only novel by Emily Brontë, published in 1847.

questions.question: Which novel features the character Jay Gatsby?
questions.explanation: Jay Gatsby is the titular character in F. Scott Fitzgerald's 'The Great Gatsby'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Lord of the Flies'?
questions.explanation: 'Lord of the Flies' is a novel by British author William Golding, published in 1954.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play contains the famous balcony scene?
questions.explanation: The famous balcony scene occurs in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn'?
questions.explanation: 'The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn' is a novel by American author Mark Twain, published in 1884.

questions.question: Which novel begins with 'Call me Ishmael'?

questions.question: Who wrote 'Jane Eyre'?
questions.explanation: 'Jane Eyre' is a novel by English writer Charlotte Brontë, published in 1847.

questions.question: Which poet wrote 'The Raven'?
questions.explanation: 'The Raven' is a narrative poem by American writer Edgar Allan Poe, published in 1845.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Of Mice and Men'?
questions.explanation: 'Of Mice and Men' is a novella by American author John Steinbeck, published in 1937.

questions.question: Which novel features the character Scout Finch?
questions.explanation: Scout Finch is the narrator and protagonist of Harper Lee's 'To Kill a Mockingbird'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Fahrenheit 451'?
questions.explanation: 'Fahrenheit 451' is a dystopian novel by American writer Ray Bradbury, published in 1953.
